alex: Observing a ~25% tail-latency regression on small-batch chat traffic after flipping the new quant-routing patch (hybrid FP8/INT8) in canary. Traces point at kernel selection/dispatch hop. :thinking:

maria: Can you paste the perf profile? is it on SM80 hosts only or across archs?

alex: Only reproduced on SM90 infra (a100-p4x?), SM80 seems fine. Quick profiler dump:
```
[profile] kernel_dispatch: 185ms
[profile] cutlass_fp8_conv: 90ms (40%)
[profile] triton_int8_gemm_fallback: 70ms (34%)
[profile] kv-cache-serialize: 18ms
[profile] batching-overhead: 7ms
```
Notice the CUTLASS path is taking most of the time after the routing decision.

jonah: hmm, are we forcing CUTLASS for FP8 on SM90? I thought we had a Triton-vectorized FP8 path that should be faster on that arch.

alex: routing table currently: if model.quant==fp8 -> prefer_cutlass=true; fallback to triton-int8 if cutlass build flags mismatch. But the canary nodes have CUTLASS built w/ SM80 flags only (we forgot SM90 flags in the image)

priya: that would explain it — CUTLASS compiled for SM80 running on SM90 can be slower due to missing optimized kernels and alignment. Also mixed precision fallback to INT8 can add conversion overhead.

maria: So two separate things: 1) arch-detection/build-flag mismatch -> slow CUTLASS; 2) our batching heuristic picks micro-batches that favor cutlass but are bad for triton's vectorization.

alex: Repro commands I used:
```
# reproduce on canary
export MODEL=redwood-8b-quant
export RUN_PROFILE=1
./run_infer --host canary-sm90 --batch-size 4 --sequence 512
```

jonah: Quick test: can you force triton route and compare? e.g. `QUANT_ROUTER_FORCE=triton ./run_infer ...`

alex: Ran that. When forcing triton-int8 route latency drops ~18% vs current hybrid. So CUTLASS path here is the problem.

priya: Two action items: (A) avoid preferring CUTLASS on nodes where cutlass binary isn't built with arch flags for the runtime GPU; (B) re-evaluate batching thresholds for short conversational tails.

maria: For (A) we should teach the arch prober to mark nodes with their supported cutlass kernels. Maybe an env var `CUTLASS_ARCHS=sm80,sm90` in the image and runtime check on startup.

jonah: Agreed. Also add a conservative canary: if cutlass reported kernel perf < triton baseline in profiler history, set prefer_cutlass=false. We already store per-node microbenchmarks in /metrics/kernel-bench.

alex: I'll put up a small PR to add runtime arch-check and a safety flag. Draft patch summary:
- runtime: probe GLIBC/CUDA arch -> advertise cutlass_archs
- quant-router: consult node.advertised_cutlass_archs before preferring cutlass
- batching: add a short_sequence_bias to favor smaller batch sizes for chat workloads

priya: Perf test checklist:
- run kernel microbench on sm90 canary images
- measure end-to-end p99 with conv-chat workload at varying batch sizes
- check KV cache hit behavior: ensure kv cache serialization isn't triggered unnecessarily when switching routes

alex: Yes — current path triggers a convert when model variant differs. That conversion is expensive. We should prefer stable route for active sessions or add an in-place conversion kernel.

jonah: Could also cache converted KV pages per route variant keyed by (session_id, route_key) to avoid repeated conversions for hot sessions.
